summary:
**PLANETARY TIME MACHINE- is an AI-assisted platform designed to discover when and where Earth's environments most closely resemble selected regions of the Moon and Mars. Instead of simply identifying places that look similar to planetary landscapes, the project compares measurable environmental characteristics such as geology, elevation, surface roughness, temperature, moisture, dust and ice conditions.

The platform brings together Earth observation data from NASA, ESA, CSA and JAXA with planetary mission data from NASA's Planetary Data System, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter observations. Its temporal analysis feature explores seasonal and historical changes to identify periods when terrestrial conditions provide stronger planetary analogues. An explainable similarity engine ranks candidate locations and displays data coverage, confidence and scientific evidence.

By helping researchers identify suitable Earth-based environments and time windows for planetary mission simulations, equipment testing and astronaut training, PLANETARY TIME MACHINE aims to make planetary exploration research more accessible, efficient and evidence-driven.
details:
PLANETARY TIME MACHINE

PLANETARY TIME MACHINE is an AI-assisted platform designed to explore when and where Earth's environments most closely resemble selected regions of the Moon and Mars. It focuses on comparing important environmental characteristics such as geology, elevation, surface roughness, temperature, moisture, dust and ice conditions to identify potential terrestrial analogue locations.

The platform is designed to let users select a planetary target, explore possible matching locations on Earth and examine environmental similarities through an interactive interface. Its time-based approach considers seasonal and historical variations to explore how environmental conditions change and when certain locations may offer stronger planetary analogues.

The project could benefit planetary scientists, researchers, students and space mission planners by helping identify suitable Earth-based environments for mission simulations, equipment testing and astronaut training. Its intended impact is to make planetary analogue discovery more accessible, efficient and data-driven.

The website was developed using Google AI Studio and AI-assisted development tools. Our team used these tools to translate our scientific concept into an interactive web-based platform. The project is designed around the use of Earth observation and planetary datasets from space agencies such as NASA, ESA, CSA and JAXA.

The creative aspect of PLANETARY TIME MACHINE is its focus on both where and when Earth resembles another planetary environment. Rather than depending only on visual similarities, the concept emphasizes measurable environmental characteristics and their changes over time. During development, we considered scientific reliability, data availability, seasonal variations, usability and the limitations of terrestrial analogues. Since Earth cannot fully reproduce conditions such as lunar vacuum, reduced gravity or the thin Martian atmosphere, the platform focuses on identifying useful environmental similarities rather than claiming exact planetary equivalence.
